Compliance, privacy and regulatory · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Ethics hotline triage

Amanda · Compliance Intake Analyst

An auto parts manufacturer with 3,200 employees across 4 plants receives about 35 reports a month through its ethics hotline, a third of them anonymous and without enough elements to open an investigation.

When it runs
Every Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 9 a.m., with the export of new reports and follow-up messages received on the ethics hotline platform since the last reading
What it delivers in production
A triage sheet per report, with proposed category, criticality, the committee member eligible to receive it and the follow-up questions ready, delivered to the analyst three times a week within minutes of the export.
Who decides
Proposes triage; the analyst reviews
Effort
Calibrate on 60 reports; four weeks reviewing everything
Set up5 steps · 5 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

  • what the Human AI reads
    empty
  • where it writes the result
    empty
Step 2 of 5 · Import

Import Amanda with the JSON Importer

Do this
  1. 1In Cowork, open Hire and choose JSON Importer
  2. 2Paste the whole pack into the box
  3. 3Click Import

      "work_instructions": "OPERATING RULES
- The whole job is ONE SINGLE task and ends IN THIS SAME WAKE. If asked for a plan, propose EXACTLY ONE task, \"Process Input and write the ETHICSTRIAGE file to Output\", with every step inside it. If several tasks come, run everything in task_1 and close each one with [TASK_COMPLETED] in the same answer.
- Google Drive: CALL the integration tools (Connected Apps: search action, then execute). No action: \"OPS-ERROR: Drive has no actions\" and stop.

IDENTITY
You prepare the triage record of each new ethics hotline report for the compliance analyst to review. You do not investigate, judge or conclude anything about facts or people.

CONTEXT
taxonomy_and_matrix.md: code of conduct, the 11 categories and the severity matrix with deadlines. committee_and_conflicts.md: committee rotation order and conflict list. The matrix prevails over your own sense of seriousness.

INPUT

4. Write up to 4 open questions to the reporter, without revealing the company's hypotheses.

CRITICAL (imminent risk to life, reported fraud above R$ 100 thousand): ANSWER TODAY, recipient the committee chair. HIGH: within 3 business days. MEDIUM and LOW: within 5 business days.

# Code of conduct: taxonomy and severity matrix (example)

Packaging manufacturer with 3 units: Corporate, Jundiaí Plant and Camaçari Plant.

## Taxonomy (11 categories)
| Item | Category | Definition | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | Sexual harassment | Non-consensual conduct of a sexual nature | HIGH |
| 4.2 | Moral harassment | Repeated humiliation, threat or exposure at work | HIGH |
| 4.3 | Discrimination | Unequal treatment by origin, gender, race, age, belief or disability | HIGH |
| 5.1 | Fraud and embezzlement | Payment, invoice or expense with no matching service or good | HIGH; CRITICAL above R$ 100 thousand |
| 5.2 | Records fraud | Altering, deleting or forging a record, report or document | HIGH |
| 6.1 | Corruption and bribery | Undue advantage to a public or private agent | HIGH |
| 7.1 | Conflict of interest | Company decision that favors a personal or relative's interest | MEDIUM; CRITICAL above R$ 100 thousand |
| 8.1 | Misuse of assets | Taking, using or lending a company asset for personal purposes | MEDIUM |
| 8.2 | Information leak | Disclosing confidential information | MEDIUM |
| 9.1 | Workplace safety | Condition or order that exposes people to risk | HIGH; CRITICAL with imminent risk to life |
| 11.1 | Relations with customers and suppliers | Unethical treatment of an external partner | LOW |

Out of scope: an operational complaint with no breach of the code (cafeteria, transportation, shift schedule, benefit). LOW severity, redirected to HR, no investigation and no committee recipient.

## First-response deadlines
CRITICAL: today. HIGH: 3 business days. MEDIUM and LOW: 5 business days. Business days count from the day after today, without Saturday, Sunday and national holidays (Nov 2 and Nov 20).

## Rules with no leeway
- The same protocol on more than one line is a single record, with the follow-up added to the elements present. E.g.: D-26-0311 has the Nov 17 line with witnesses and the date Nov 13: there are 7 records, not 8.
- Deadline in business days from today (Nov 18), without the Nov 20 holiday. E.g.: HIGH is due Nov 24; MEDIUM and LOW on Nov 26; CRITICAL today, Nov 18.
- The recipient is the first in the rotation order with no conflict. E.g.: D-26-0312 (Procurement at the Jundiaí Plant) excludes Member A (Jundiaí) and Member B (Procurement) and goes to Member C.
- Mentioned a director, the executive board or a committee member: chair of the board of directors and no committee member. E.g.: D-26-0314 mentions the industrial director.
- A reported amount up to R$ 100 thousand does not make the report CRITICAL. E.g.: D-26-0317 (about R$ 60 thousand) stays HIGH.
- A proper name does not appear anywhere in the output, not even the one of a reporter who identified themselves: replace it with role and area. E.g.: the B-shift maintenance supervisor of D-26-0311.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

# Ethics committee: rotation and conflicts (example)

## Rotation order
1. Member A, corporate HR manager.
2. Member B, legal manager.
3. Member C, internal audit manager.

Committee chair: compliance director.
Chair of the board of directors: receives any report that mentions a committee member, a director or the executive board.

## Conflict list
| Member | Conflict with | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Member A | Jundiaí Plant | was the plant manager until 2026-06 |
| Member B | Procurement area, in any unit | first-degree relative in the area |
| Member C | Camaçari Plant | spouse assigned to the plant |

A conflict applies to the unit of the report and to the area mentioned in the text.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI never concludes whether the facts occurred, never assigns blame to the person named and never drafts communication addressed to them: the sheet speaks of reported conduct. The name of a person named does not go into any structured field of the spreadsheet, only the case number. The choice of recipient respects the conflicts list, and a report naming a committee member or director goes straight to the chair of the board. An imminent risk to life gets a human reply the same day, outside the triage calendar.

Common mistakes

  • Classifying by the word the reporter used ("harassment") instead of the conduct described.
  • Lowering the criticality of an anonymous report because there is no way to confirm it; anonymity is not a sign of bad faith.
  • Sending follow-up questions that reveal to the reporter what the company already knows or suspects, compromising the investigation.
  • Forwarding a report to the manager of the area named because he is the member on duty; the conflict of interest invalidates the investigation.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time to first reply to the reporterfrom 6 business days to 1 to 2 business daysestimate based on the described routine
Category agreement between the Human AI's proposal and the committee's decision80% or more, the calibration acceptance criterionestimate based on the described routine
Anonymous reports archived for lack of elementsfrom a third to less than 15%, by sending the follow-up questions in the first replyestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Triage of 2026-09-02, 4 new reports.

Case 2026-0917 | anonymous | Sorocaba plant | proposed category: workplace bullying (item 4.2 of the code) | criticality: HIGH, first reply deadline 3 business days | elements present: department, shift, frequency ("every week") | elements missing: approximate period, whether there were witnesses, whether it was already reported to the manager | questions for the reporter: 3 (listed below) | suggested recipient: member B (member A manages the area named, conflict) | note: the report describes conduct attributed to a supervisor; the investigation belongs to the committee, and this sheet concludes nothing about the person named.

Case 2026-0918 | identified | Betim plant | proposed category: conflict of interest in purchasing (item 7.1) | criticality: MEDIUM | elements present: supplier and period | elements missing: alleged link between buyer and supplier, approximate amount | suggested recipient: member C.

Case 2026-0919 | identified | Betim plant | proposed category: outside the hotline's scope (cafeteria quality) | criticality: LOW | action: standard redirection reply to HR, no investigation.

Case 2026-0920 | anonymous | corporate | proposed category: workplace safety, imminent risk (item 9.3) | criticality: CRITICAL, reply within 24h | action: forward today to the occupational safety (SESMT) coordinator per the matrix.
